title: European Council Conclusions from the 21-22 March 2024 Meeting on Ukraine, Security, Middle East, Enlargement, and EU Policies
executive_summary: The European Council meeting on 21-22 March 2024 focused on key global challenges, notably the ongoing war in Ukraine, security and defense, the Middle East conflict, enlargement, and external relations. The Council reaffirmed unwavering support for Ukraine’s sovereignty, committing intensified military, financial, and humanitarian aid, and called for stronger sanctions against Russia and its allies. It emphasized enhancing EU defense capabilities, industrial base, and readiness, complementing NATO. On the Middle East, the Council condemned Hamas, urged a humanitarian pause in Gaza, and supported a two-state solution. Enlargement discussions included opening accession talks with Bosnia and Herzegovina and progress on Ukraine, Moldova, and Georgia. The Council addressed migration, agriculture, crisis preparedness, and economic policy, endorsing sustainable growth priorities. It also expressed concern over human rights in Russia and Belarus, and instability in Haiti, calling for political solutions and international cooperation.
characteristics: The European Council reaffirmed strong support for Ukraine's sovereignty, providing extensive political, financial, military, and humanitarian aid amid ongoing Russian aggression.
Emphasis on enhancing EU defense capabilities, increasing defense spending, and strengthening the European defense industrial base to address rising security threats.
Urgent call for humanitarian pause and ceasefire in the Middle East, condemning violence and stressing respect for international law and human rights.
Commitment to EU enlargement with accession talks opened for Bosnia and Herzegovina, and progress noted for Ukraine, Moldova, and Georgia.
Focus on migration control, countering human trafficking and smuggling, and launching a Global Alliance to address these challenges.
Support for sustainable agriculture, farmers' income stability, and addressing challenges in the food supply chain and trade measures related to Ukraine.

Political Actors: European Union Police Mission for the Palestinian Territories (EUPOL COPPS)
European Union Border Assistance Mission to the Rafah Crossing Point (EUBAM Rafah)

practical_applications: The European Union is providing Ukraine with comprehensive political, financial, economic, humanitarian, military, and diplomatic support, including speeding up delivery of air defence systems, ammunition, and missiles.
The EU has adopted a Council Decision regarding a Ukraine Assistance Fund to continue military support under the European Peace Facility and is working on the 8th support package.
The EU Military Assistance Mission (EUMAM) capacity has been increased to support Ukraine.
The European Council supports efforts to direct extraordinary revenues from Russia’s immobilised assets to benefit Ukraine, including funding military support.
The EU has adopted the 13th package of sanctions against Russia and is preparing further sanctions against Belarus, North Korea, and Iran.
The EU is prepared to respond with restrictive measures against Iran if it transfers ballistic missiles or related technology to Russia.
The European Union Advisory Mission (EUAM) in Ukraine has been strengthened to support law enforcement and reforms.
The EU is providing psychological and psychosocial rehabilitation support and increased demining assistance in Ukraine.
The EU is assisting Ukraine in rebuilding its export markets, especially in the Middle East and Africa.
The EU supports the Republic of Moldova and Georgia in strengthening resilience, security, and stability, including through the European Union Partnership Mission (EUPM) in Moldova.

The European Union is committed to increasing defence readiness and capabilities, including fulfilling commitments to increase defence expenditure, improving access to finance for the defence industry, incentivising joint procurement, and enhancing the European defence industrial base.

The European Council invites the Council and Commission to explore funding options for defence and to advance the European Defence Industrial Strategy (EDIS) and European Defence Industry Programme (EDIP).

The EU is implementing the Strategic Compass, focusing on rapid deployment capacity, military mobility, live exercises, space security, cyber and hybrid threat countermeasures, and foreign information manipulation and interference.
The EU launched the Amalthea Initiative to open a maritime route for emergency assistance from Cyprus to Gaza, supplementing land routes.

The EU supports the two CSDP missions in the Palestinian Territories: the European Union Police Mission for the Palestinian Territories (EUPOL COPPS) and the European Union Border Assistance Mission to the Rafah Crossing Point (EUBAM Rafah).
The EU is working on further restrictive measures against Hamas and extremist settler violence in the West Bank.
The EU launched Operation ASPIDES to safeguard freedom of navigation and security of seafarers in the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden, and broader region.
The EU has released EUR 20 million in humanitarian support to Haiti and supports the UN Security Council Resolution 2699 for a Multinational Security Support Mission.
The EU supports a comprehensive approach to migration, including strengthening tools to counter human trafficking and smuggling and launching a Global Alliance to address these challenges.

The EU is working on short- and medium-term measures to support farmers, including reducing administrative burdens, strengthening farmers’ position in the food supply chain, providing additional financial support, ensuring fair competition, and addressing trade measures related to Ukraine.
The EU is advancing work on enhanced and coordinated military and civilian preparedness and strategic crisis management, with a view to a future preparedness strategy.
The European Council has decided to open accession negotiations with Bosnia and Herzegovina and is advancing accession frameworks for Ukraine, Moldova, and Georgia.
The EU welcomes joint declarations and partnerships with Egypt and Mauritania to strengthen strategic and comprehensive partnerships.
commitments: The EU is committed to providing Ukraine with one million rounds of artillery ammunition.
The European Council calls on the Council to work on the 8th support package for Ukraine under the European Peace Facility.
The European Council invites the Council and the Commission to explore all options for mobilising funding for the European defence industry and report back by June 2024.
The European Council will adopt conclusions on a roadmap for future work on internal reforms by summer 2024.
The European Council decides to open accession negotiations with Bosnia and Herzegovina once all relevant steps set out in the Commission’s recommendation of 12 October 2022 are taken.
The European Council invites the Council to swiftly adopt the draft negotiating frameworks for Ukraine and the Republic of Moldova and to take work forward without delay.
The European Council welcomes the recent release by the European Union of EUR 20 million in humanitarian support to Haiti.
The European Council calls on the Commission and the High Representative to take necessary steps to prevent the execution by third countries of arrest warrants issued by Russia against EU citizens.

The European Council calls on the Commission and the Council to take work forward without delay on short- and medium-term measures to support farmers, including extending the temporary framework on State aid, and report back to the next European Council.

The European Council invites the Council to take work forward and the Commission together with the High Representative to propose actions to strengthen preparedness and crisis response at EU level with a view to a future preparedness strategy.

kpi_list.target_description: Provide Ukraine with one million rounds of artillery ammunition
kpi_list.measurement_method: Tracking delivery and receipt of ammunition rounds

kpi_list.kpi_text: The European Council calls on the Council to work on the 8th support package for Ukraine under the European Peace Facility
kpi_list.target_description: Develop and approve the 8th support package for Ukraine under the European Peace Facility
kpi_list.measurement_method: Adoption and implementation of the support package

kpi_list.kpi_text: The European Council calls for further steps to weaken Russia’s ability to continue waging its war of aggression, including by strengthening the sanctions. Full and effective implementation of sanctions is essential.
kpi_list.metric_name: Strengthening and Implementation of Sanctions Against Russia
kpi_list.target_description: Strengthen sanctions and ensure full and effective implementation to weaken Russia's war capabilities
kpi_list.measurement_method: Monitoring sanctions enforcement and closing loopholes

kpi_list.kpi_text: The European Council supports ongoing efforts, including in the Core Group, to establish a tribunal for the prosecution of the crime of aggression against Ukraine that would enjoy the broadest cross-regional support and legitimacy, and a future compensation mechanism.
kpi_list.metric_name: Establishment of Tribunal for Crime of Aggression Against Ukraine
kpi_list.target_description: Establish a tribunal with broad cross-regional support for prosecuting crimes of aggression against Ukraine and set up a compensation mechanism
kpi_list.measurement_method: Creation and operationalization of tribunal and compensation mechanism

kpi_list.kpi_text: The European Council welcomes the recent strengthening of the European Union Advisory Mission (EUAM) in Ukraine which will allow the scaling up of support for Ukrainian law enforcement agencies in Ukraine’s liberated and adjacent territories, and for reforms in the context of its EU accession process.
kpi_list.metric_name: Scaling Up EUAM Support for Ukrainian Law Enforcement and Reforms
kpi_list.target_description: Scale up support for Ukrainian law enforcement agencies and reforms linked to EU accession
kpi_list.measurement_method: Monitoring EUAM activities and reform progress

kpi_list.kpi_text: The European Council calls for further support for psychological and psychosocial rehabilitation and for increased demining assistance.
kpi_list.metric_name: Support for Psychological Rehabilitation and Demining in Ukraine
kpi_list.target_description: Increase support for psychological and psychosocial rehabilitation and demining assistance in Ukraine
kpi_list.measurement_method: Tracking support programs and assistance delivered

kpi_list.kpi_text: The European Council calls for an immediate humanitarian pause leading to a sustainable ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages and the provision of humanitarian assistance.
kpi_list.metric_name: Humanitarian Pause and Ceasefire in Middle East Conflict
kpi_list.target_description: Achieve an immediate humanitarian pause, sustainable ceasefire, unconditional release of hostages, and provision of humanitarian aid
kpi_list.measurement_method: Verification of ceasefire, hostage release, and aid delivery
kpi_list.responsible_entity: All parties involved in the Middle East conflict

kpi_list.kpi_text: The European Council calls on the Council to accelerate work on the adoption of further relevant restrictive measures against Hamas.
kpi_list.metric_name: Adoption of Restrictive Measures Against Hamas
kpi_list.target_description: Accelerate adoption of further restrictive measures targeting Hamas
kpi_list.measurement_method: Adoption and enforcement of restrictive measures

kpi_list.kpi_text: The European Council invites the Council and the Commission to explore all options for mobilising funding and report back by June.
kpi_list.metric_name: Funding Mobilisation for European Defence Industry
kpi_list.target_description: Explore all options for mobilising funding for the European defence industry and report back
kpi_list.measurement_method: Submission of report on funding options

kpi_list.kpi_text: The European Council will address internal reforms at an upcoming meeting with a view to adopting by summer 2024 conclusions on a roadmap for future work.
kpi_list.metric_name: Adoption of Roadmap for Internal Reforms
kpi_list.target_description: Adopt conclusions on a roadmap for internal reforms to prepare the EU for enlargement
kpi_list.measurement_method: Adoption of conclusions at European Council meeting

top_actors.name: European Council
top_actors.justification: The European Council is the primary actor in the document, as it is the body adopting the conclusions and driving the discussions on all key topics including Ukraine, security and defence, Middle East, enlargement, and external relations. It is mentioned throughout the text as the decision-making and coordinating entity.

top_actors.name: European Union
top_actors.justification: The European Union is central to the document’s context, representing the collective entity providing political, financial, military, and humanitarian support, especially to Ukraine and other partner countries. The EU’s institutions and missions are frequently referenced as implementing and supporting the Council’s decisions.

top_actors.name: Ukraine
top_actors.justification: Ukraine is a key focus of the document, with extensive references to the war of aggression against it, the EU’s support, military assistance, sanctions against Russia, and reconstruction efforts. Ukraine’s sovereignty and security are central to the European Council’s agenda and actions.

top_themes.name: Multilateralism (Regional & International Cooperation)
top_themes.justification: The document heavily focuses on international cooperation, geopolitical challenges, and partnerships, especially regarding Ukraine, Russia, the Middle East, enlargement, and global security. Multilateralism is central to the EU's strategic approach and commitments throughout the conclusions.

top_themes.name: Technology Regulations (Technology & Innovation)
top_themes.justification: While the document mentions strengthening the European defence technological and industrial base and related investments, direct references to technology regulations or innovation governance are limited and mostly linked to defence capabilities rather than broader digital governance.

top_themes.name: Digital Governance (Data & Governance)
top_themes.justification: The document does not explicitly address digital governance or data-related issues. Any indirect references are minimal and overshadowed by the focus on security, defence, and geopolitical matters.
